example.name: Neighbourhood Table
example.problem: Busy people want affordable, healthy meals but have little time to cook.
example.solution: A local platform connecting home cooks with neighbours who want fresh, ready-made meals.
example.users: Busy professionals and students living in urban neighbourhoods.

reviewers.name: Alex Morgan
reviewers.description: Turn a promising concept into a business that makes sense. Pressure-test your market, pricing, and path to growth.

reviewers.name: Sam Chen
reviewers.description: Find a practical path from idea to build. Explore feasibility, technical risks, and what your first version really needs.

reviewers.name: Jordan Ellis
reviewers.description: See your idea through your users’ eyes. Challenge assumptions and shape an experience people will want to use.

business.summary: A clear everyday problem and a focused audience give this concept a useful starting point. The next step is to test demand before investing in a full product.
strengths: Starts with a recognisable, recurring customer problem.
A focused initial audience makes early interviews easier.
The core proposition can be tested with a small manual pilot.

weaknesses.title: Demand is still an assumption
weaknesses.why: A problem can be real without customers being willing to pay for a new solution.
weaknesses.improvement: Interview five target users about their most recent experience. Ask what they tried and what it cost.

weaknesses.title: The business model needs a first test
weaknesses.why: Acquisition and delivery costs can outweigh revenue even when people like the idea.
weaknesses.improvement: Map the costs of serving one customer and test one price with a small pilot.

weaknesses.title: The difference from alternatives is unclear
weaknesses.why: People need a compelling reason to switch from their current workaround.
weaknesses.improvement: Compare three existing alternatives and write one specific reason your audience would choose you.

tasks: Map the cost of serving one customer
Run a small pilot before building

technical.summary: The concept can start small. Focus on a single end-to-end journey, validate it manually, and use what you learn to decide what to automate.
strengths: The main problem can be explored without a complex platform.
A defined audience helps prioritise the first user journey.
A manual pilot can uncover requirements before development.

weaknesses.title: The first release has no clear boundary
weaknesses.why: Building every feature early delays the learning that matters most.
weaknesses.improvement: Choose one user journey and list the minimum steps needed to complete it.

weaknesses.title: Data handling is not yet defined
weaknesses.why: Collecting unnecessary personal data increases implementation and privacy risk.
weaknesses.improvement: List the data required at each step and remove anything the pilot does not need.

weaknesses.title: Failure cases are unexplored
weaknesses.why: Missing or incorrect information can stop users from completing the core task.
weaknesses.improvement: Sketch what happens when an input is invalid, a request fails, or a user leaves midway.

tasks: Test the workflow with a manual pilot

ux.summary: The idea starts from a relatable need. Make the intended experience more concrete by observing real users and testing a short prototype before building.
strengths: The concept addresses an everyday user need.
The intended audience is specific enough to recruit research participants.
The value proposition can be explored in a lightweight prototype.

weaknesses.title: The audience still contains different needs
weaknesses.why: Users with different routines may need very different experiences.
weaknesses.improvement: Pick one initial user group and document the situation in which they need help.

weaknesses.title: The first-use experience is undefined
weaknesses.why: People may leave if they cannot quickly understand what to do and what they will get.
weaknesses.improvement: Sketch three screens showing the shortest path from arrival to the first useful result.

weaknesses.title: Trust has not been tested
weaknesses.why: Unanswered questions can prevent people from trying an unfamiliar service.
weaknesses.improvement: Ask five users what would make them hesitate, then test copy that addresses those concerns.
